code.stream_ids_filter: operational shard filter applied after validate_formal_inputs; not a fourth scientific factor; checkpoint identity does not include the stream list

control.must_match: At budget 28672, repository-macro DUF and the delayed-edge retained set of Age-only and Oracle-Future match both m1a_v4 and m1a_v8, and RACC-TFIDF matches m1a_v8. Expected repository-macro DUF: Age-only 0.6428571428571429, RACC-TFIDF 0.6904761904761905, Oracle-Future 1.0. Any mismatch stops the campaign before E2 or E3.

e1.evaluator: import evaluate() from the unmodified m1a_evaluate.py and pass budgets=[28672]. The CLI refuses because it requires budgets == [28672, 57344]. The evaluator file is not modified.
e1.question: q1

extra.crossed_compression_delayed_edges: A delayed edge crosses a compression for an arm when at least one trigger on that stream, arm, and budget has decision group index D with origin_group_index < D <= consume_group_index. D is the group_index of the trigger's decision_action_event_id in groups.jsonl. The condensation is evaluated immediately before that decision action, so a trigger on the consume group counts.
extra.paired_repository_difference: For each repository with delayed edges, repository DUF(arm) minus repository DUF(reference). Report every repository and the unweighted mean. Also report that mean after dropping dstl/Stone-Soup. Reference is the same Age-only used for the token relative difference.
extra.prefix_excluded_wipe: Only prefix_excluded arms, only triggers whose reasons include tokens. C_t = (B - |P|) // 2. A compressible unit is a live source group or generated summary that does not intersect keep_first. A wipe deletes every compressible unit. Zero compressible units is not a wipe. A forced wipe is a wipe in which every compressible unit has tokens > C_t. Wipe rate = wipe triggers / token-reason triggers on prefix_excluded arms. Also report the forced-wipe count.
extra.protection_and_over_target: For every trigger, protected_tokens is the sum of marginal tokens of groups admitted to the protection set before fire-line sacrifice. tokens_over_target is max(0, retained_tokens_before_summary - target) after deletion, including fire-line sacrifice. Report the median and the maximum per arm and budget. Median of an even count is the mean of the two central values.
extra.token_relative_difference_on_disagreemen: Within one target rule, a stream disagrees at a budget when the delayed-edge retained bit vector differs across the arms that use that target rule. E1 therefore has a half_budget set and a prefix_excluded set; the two targets are not pooled. E3's set also includes E2 Age-only at the same budget, so a stream counts when Oracle-H8, Oracle-H8-quota, or Age-only differ. Token relative difference of an arm versus the reference is (mean decision-view history tokens of the arm on that stream minus the reference) divided by the reference. The reported value is the unweighted mean of those per-stream ratios. Reference is Age-only of the same target rule inside E1, Age-only inside E2, and E2 Age-only for E3.

oracle_horizon.distance: first consume_group_index >= decision_group_index; distance = consume - decision + 1; risk is 1 iff 1 <= distance <= horizon, else 0
oracle_horizon.label_check: When horizon is 8, every row must agree with frozen label_now OR label_soon OR label_later. A mismatch aborts before replay.

not_hashed: this protocol's pre-replay sha256 file is the required pre-replay hash and is not an extra category

questions.gates: none. These questions are reported as numbers. A result that does not support the motivating hypothesis is reported as the number, not as a failure.
questions.q1: Under prefix_excluded, are the repository-macro DUF differences of RACC-TFIDF-rank and Oracle-rank versus Age-only-prefix larger than the same differences of RACC-TFIDF-rank and Oracle-rank versus Age-only under half_budget? Report all four differences and the two comparisons. Budget 28672 only.
questions.q2: At Q=6144 and half_budget, at each of 28672 and 57344, report repository-macro DUF of TFIDF-quota and Oracle-quota minus Age-quota, minus each Random-quota seed (20261001, 20261002, 20261003), and minus the unweighted mean of the three random repository-macro DUFs.
questions.q3: How many delayed edges does Oracle-H8 fail to retain that Oracle-Future retains? Also report the reverse count and the net (Oracle-Future retained count minus Oracle-H8 retained count). At 28672 the Oracle-Future arm is the E1 half_budget rerun. At 57344 E1 did not rerun Oracle-Future, so the reference is m1a_v8 Oracle-Future, which m1a_v4 matches on the delayed retained set. Oracle-H8-quota is reported in the tables and is not this comparison.

quota.admission: At each trigger, walk deletable original groups in this arm's own high-to-low order. Add a group if and only if cumulative tokens plus that group's tokens are <= Q. The first group that would exceed Q is not added, and the walk stops. Later smaller groups are not considered.
quota.applies_to: age, score, and random arms that set protect_quota_tokens. Mutually exclusive with protect_min_risk and protect_top_k.

justification.excluded_from_quota_selection: dev split, including zurutech/ashpy origin 27 source_tokens 1083
justification.origin: dstl/Stone-Soup origin group_index 59, train split, two delayed edges, budget 28672, source_tokens from formal_dataset_v7 groups.jsonl
justification.why_6144: The task specifies Q=6144. 6144 = 12 * 512, so it is a multiple of 512, and 6144 >= 5517, so it covers that train origin. It is not the least such multiple; the least multiple of 512 that covers 5517 is 5632. This protocol does not retune Q and does not claim that 6144 equals ceil(5517/512)*512.

quota.outside_protection: Groups outside the protection set are deleted in the arm's original deletion order until the target is met. The fire line still applies.

sort_keys.random_score: sha256(f'{seed}\x1f{stream_id}\x1f{group_id}') first 8 bytes / 2^64, stable per group, not per decision
sort_keys.score_protection: reverse of deletion, highest risk first, then newer group_index

quota.unit: Marginal production tokens of each contiguous live source group in the current view: count(view[:end]) - count(view[:start]), the same difference-of-prefixes definition as dataset source_tokens. Summaries are not quota-protected.

shard_balance: Four shards. Streams were bin-packed by Age-only trigger count summed over budgets 28672 and 57344 in replay_v10 (total weight 120, 30 per shard). All shards use the single endpoint above. At most 4 replay processes run at once.

pass_requires: each smoke replay exits 0 and writes REPLAY_COMPLETE with the expected run count
half_budget Age-only, RACC-TFIDF, and Oracle-Future delayed-edge retention on these two streams matches m1a_v4 and m1a_v8
on token triggers, prefix_excluded target equals |P|+(B-|P|)//2 and is greater than B//2 when |P|>0
quota arms record protected_tokens, and at least one Stone-Soup quota trigger has protected_tokens > 0
Oracle-H8 loads the horizon-8 score file
smoke.why: django-rest-email-auth holds the train Age-drop/Oracle-keep origin 1. Stone-Soup holds origins 2 and 59, including the 5517-token origin that sets the quota.

target_rules.fire_line: After the target pass, if retained tokens exceed B - 4096, protected source groups are sacrificed lowest-priority first until retained tokens are at or under that line. keep_first events are never deleted.
target_rules.half_budget: When the SDK trigger reasons include tokens, target = B // 2. Otherwise target is the token count of the events the SDK itself would have retained. This is the historical rule.
target_rules.prefix_excluded: Only for policy age, score, or random, and only when reasons include tokens: |P| is the production token count of the first keep_first events in the current view; target = |P| + (B - |P|) // 2. Non-token triggers keep the historical SDK retained-count target. Default-Recency is not modified and is not an arm in this protocol.

technical_failures: Disconnects, OOM, and cascade-limit errors are not results. The completed checkpoint units are kept and the failed unit is rerun with --resume after the cause is fixed.
